title: A High-Precision and Low-Cost Approximate Transform Accelerator for Video Coding
problem: The Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard introduces multiple transform types (DCT2, DST7) requiring separate hardware implementations, leading to substantial circuit overhead and duplicated area. Efficient reuse of shared transform infrastructure while maintaining codec precision remains challenging.
motivation: Modern video coding standards demand higher compression efficiency, but transform diversity in VVC increases hardware complexity. Reducing area and power without quality loss is essential for real-time video acceleration.
method: The work exploits diagonal aggregation properties in DCT2-to-DST7 transfer matrices and applies least-squares optimization to sparsify these matrices. A lightweight matrix decomposition strategy enables a single shift-adder unit to generate product terms for multiple transform sizes (4–32 points), supporting three VVC transform types through reusable hardware.
key_novelty: Discovery of diagonal aggregation phenomenon in transform transfer matrices enables high-precision approximate conversion between DCT2 and DST7 using sparse linear combinations.
contributions: Systematic analysis revealing diagonal aggregation property in DCT2–DST7 transfer matrices
Least-squares matrix sparsification method achieving 44% area reduction with 0.53% BD-BR loss
Unified, reusable approximate transform accelerator supporting multiple VVC transform types and sizes
Validation on 8K video encoding at 57 fps with minimal quality degradation
baselines: Separate DCT2 and DST7 circuit implementations
limitations: Evaluation focuses only on VVC; applicability to other video standards or future codecs not discussed.
primary_theme: Reusable approximate transform hardware for unified video codec acceleration
